articles.title: Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if US agrees to demands
articles.summary:
Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if US agrees to demands

Iran on Monday said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington agrees to conditions, as US President Donald Trump issued his latest war threat at a rally for midterm elections.

A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed "good faith".

Tehran has blockaded Hormuz since the war started in February, sending energy prices soaring and posing an electoral challenge for Trump. The narrow gateway to the energy-rich Gulf normally carries one-fifth of global oil consumption.

"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach," foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.

Reporting by AFP

articles.title: London police arrest man over posters showing 'monstrous' photo of armed Israeli
articles.summary:
London police arrest man over posters showing 'monstrous' photo of armed Israeli

Submitted by Elis Gjevori on Mon, 11/02/2026 - 12:38
The posters used an infamous but authentic photograph of a man in military uniform jeering at a Palestinian woman in the occupied West Bank
L'Espresso's image edited and depicting the Israeli settler threatening Palestinians in the occupied West Bank (L'Espresso/Pietro Masturzo)
Off

London police have arrested a man over posters depicting an armed Israeli settler jeering at a Palestinian woman in the occupied West Bank after a complaint into its allegedly antisemitic connotations.

The posters, which carried the caption “Labour’s monsters”, showed an armed man in military uniform taunting a Palestinian woman.

Italian photojournalist Pietro Masturzo took the photograph in the occupied Palestinian village of Idhna, west of Hebron, on 12 October 2025 - the first day of the olive harvest.

Masturzo’s photograph appeared in the April edition of L’Espresso, alongside reports on the expansion of Israel’s settler movement and its impact on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

“The settler's expression is reflected in the gesture he repeats, mimicking the sound a shepherd makes when gathering his flock, addressing the Palestinians as if they were his own animals,” the photojournalist said.

The magazine also reported testimonies from Palestinians in the Jordan Valley, where settlers, often backed by Israeli forces, carry out near-daily attacks.

Police investigated the posters, which appeared around London during local elections in May. They were put up in protest at Labour’s support for Israel during the Gaza genocide.

'Stirs up hatred against Jewish people '

The investigation was triggered after a complaint filed to the police. According to The Daily Telegraph, the complaint described the image as a “monstrous characterisation” of a Jewish man.

The complainant also said the photograph was “selected to appear menacing”.

The unidentified complainant also claimed that the image was “anchored specifically in Jewish religious identity markers, not Israeli military conduct generally. This stirs up hatred against Jewish people.”

According to the complaint, the posters appeared to “frame the Labour Party as acting in the service of Israeli government policy” and that “Labour are complicit in genocide”.

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said: “On Thursday, Oct 1, a 36-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of a racially aggravated public order offence following an incident in May, 2026, in which a number of anti-Semitic posters were displayed across Tower Hamlets. He was released on bail pending further inquiries.”

In September, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband described attacks by Jewish settlers as “terrorism” supported by the Israeli state and said settlers were responsible for ethnic cleansing in the West Bank.

Jordan's King Abdullah said there would be no security in the Middle East until the Palestinians' right to "their homeland" is fulfilled.

"We reiterate, time and again, that there can be no security or stability in our region without upholding the Palestinian people's right to their homeland," he said at the opening of Jordan's parliament.
